articles.title: ‘This should be condemned by any thinking human’: film industry rallies behind NAZA directors
articles.summary: Backing comes after Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor were threatened with having their citizenship revoked and accused of treason. Film industry heavyweights across the globe have expressed solidarity with Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, the Oscar-winning Israeli directors of documentary NAZA, who have…
body: NAZA, which was produced by the Guardian, is named for an acronym euphemistically used by Israel’s intelligence service to indicate how many civilians it expects to die in an airstrike on Gaza. It includes interviews with 24 Israeli military or intelligence soldiers and officers who outlined the AI-powered targeting systems used to bombard Gaza, resulting in the mass killing of Palestinian civilians.
The film builds on revelations first published by the Israeli-Palestinian publication +972 Magazine, the Hebrew-language outlet Local Call and the Guardian between 2023 and 2025.

The 80-minute documentary won the special jury prize at this year’s Venice film festival on Saturday, after receiving a 25-minute standing ovation – a festival record. On Sunday, Israel’s culture minister, Miki Zohar, accused the directors of being willing to “harm their homeland in order to receive applause from antisemites around the world”.
“I will act immediately to revoke the Israeli citizenship of these despicable creators for treason against the state,” Zohar wrote on X.

articles.title: Ed Sheeran Opener Aaron Rowe Pulls Out of Tour After Macklemore Dropped: ‘I Cannot Allow Billionaires to Silence Rightful Voices’
articles.summary: Singer-songwriter Aaron Rowe has dropped out as an opener on the North American leg of Ed Sheeran’s Loop tour after fellow supporting act Macklemore was dismissed for voicing his support for Palestine.
body: Rowe’s departure from the Loop tour comes after Macklemore was kicked off following forceful “free Palestine” comments made while opening for Sheeran at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey on Sept. 4 and 5. Macklemore released a statement on Monday in which he accused billionaire New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft of rallying fellow stadium owners to ban the rapper from the tour due to his comments.

Sheeran himself weighed in on Tuesday morning, explaining that he had nothing to do with the decision to eject Macklemore from the tour and that it had been at the discretion of the promoters and venues. He explained that he preferred to remain publicly neutral on political issues and that he is “not complicit” in doing so.

articles.title: Karina Longworth on ‘The Bisexuals,’ the Latest Season of Her ‘You Must Remember This’ Podcast: ‘Even Progressive People’ Say ‘Bisexuality is a Myth’
articles.summary: Karina Longworth isn’t that interested in modern Hollywood anymore. After 18 seasons of her “You Must Remember This” podcast, former film critic Longworth says she doesn’t pay much attention to the industry.
body: Before the launch of “The Bisexuals,” Longworth spoke with Variety about the season and her upcoming fall tour.

I just keep finding stories that I want to tell. I feel like the older I get, the less I’m interested in contemporary Hollywood. I used to be somebody that would go to the movies two or three times a week, and I don’t do that anymore. I probably see 10 or 12 new movies a year, and I have replaced that by watching so much stuff from classical Hollywood. Every time that I read a new book, I get new ideas, and then I want to watch all the movies discussed in the book, and then that leads me down these rabbit holes. I’ll keep doing the podcast until I either run out of ideas or nobody wants to listen to it anymore.

articles.title: Quentin Tarantino to Publish ‘Cliff Booth’ Novel Before Brad Pitt and David Fincher’s Movie Streams on Netflix
articles.summary: Quentin Tarantino is writing a novel version of his “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood” spinoff “Cliff Booth.” It will debut later this year, timed to the release of the forthcoming film starring Brad Pitt, who reprises his Oscar-winning role as a longtime stuntman.
body: “Cliff Booth,” both the novel and movie, take place in Hollywood, 1977 — eight years after the original story. In “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood,” Leonardo DiCaprio and Pitt portray an aging actor and his longtime stunt double who are struggling to find their place in show biz. Paying tribute to the golden age of Hollywood, “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood” was set in the late 1960s against the backdrop of the Manson family murders, with Margot Robbie playing Sharon Tate, the up-and-coming actress married to director Roman Polanski.

Sony released “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood,” which was a critical and commercial hit. The movie earned more than $400 million at worldwide box office against a $90 million budget, in addition to 10 Oscar nominations and two wins. Netflix is producing the sequel, which carries a $200 million production budget.

Tarantino decided against directing “Cliff Booth” because he’s long expressed a desire to retire after making 10 movies. He’s made nine already — “Pulp Fiction,” “Inglourious Basterds” and “Reservoir Dogs” among them — and he didn’t want a sequel to be his last.
points: Quentin Tarantino is writing a novel version of his “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood” spinoff “Cliff Booth.
It will debut later this year, timed to the release of the forthcoming film starring Brad Pitt, who reprises his Oscar-winning role as a longtime stuntman.

articles.title: Thailand Film and Tourist Officials on the Rise of Thai Cinema, Global Productions and the Impact of ‘The White Lotus’
articles.summary: Following a spike in popularity for Thailand’s film and TV industry, the country’s filmmakers and tourism officials want to make sure it lasts. Nithee Seeprae, Cod Satrusayang, Raymond Phathanavirangoon and Banjong Pisanthanakun joined Variety at the Toronto International Film Festival to discuss…
body: Pisanthanakun, whose latest film “Inherit” debuted at TIFF, is one of the filmmakers helping to introduce Thai cinema to audiences around the globe. “It’s one of the best film festivals in the world, and I’m so excited that my film got the chance to premiere [at TIFF],” Pisanthanakun said during the Variety Global Conversation. “It’s a big opportunity for Thai horror.”

Pisanthanakun is considered one of the defining voices of contemporary Thai cinema, with his film “Pee Mak” as the country’s highest-grossing title of all time. Pisanthanakun’s movies, plus films like “How to Make Millions Before Grandma Dies,” have further established the country’s presence in the international film industry. The latter became the first Thai film shortlisted at the Oscars for Best International Film.

Phathanavirangoon, the producer and founder of the SEAFIC Script Lab, says he’s noticed a new energy among Thai filmmakers, pointing to the rise of international productions coming to Thailand, such as “The Creator” and “Jurassic World: Rebirth,” as well as the country’s homegrown films.

articles.title: The Debut review – Julianne Moore is a thrill in Jesse Eisenberg’s oddball comedy
articles.summary: Toronto film festival: riotous lead performance holds together third movie from actor turned film-maker, about a housewife who joins a local musical. Jesse Eisenberg’s last two directorial efforts – the prickly comedy When You Finish Saving the World and the slightly softer A Real Pain – are small…
body: The Debut is about a repressed housewife, Mona (Julianne Moore), who decides to audition for a role in a community theater production of a musical called Nosy Neighbors, one of those gassy Manhattan trifles that were so ubiquitous on Broadway a half century ago. Mona’s kids are about to fly the nest, and her husband barely seems to notice her when she’s standing right next to him. So why not have a little creative adventure?

From that setup, Eisenberg could have gone to the obvious place, staging a sweet dramedy about a humble act of artistic expression opening Mona’s eyes to all the possibility of life outside her little bubble. He does do that, in part, but he also wants to take things to a darker place. The film gradually morphs into a study of actorly obsession and vanity, as Mona takes the Stanislavksi-esque teachings of the play’s director, Jerry (Paul Giamatti, doing his wearily charming thing), to extremes perhaps not seen since Black Swan. That’s a clever idea: a director watching in horror as the monster he’s created threatens to lay waste to his production.

articles.title: Venice best actress winner says she signed on at Danish job centre days before her victory
articles.summary: Mathilde Arcel, who won the Volpi Cup on Saturday for her role in Golden Lion winner Woman Unknown, said job offers have now begun to arrive. The winner of this year’s best actress prize at the Venice film festival has revealed that she is on unemployment benefits and had to fly to back to…
body: On Saturday night, Danish actor Mathilde Arcel won the prestigious Volpi Cup for her first leading role in a feature film, May el-Toukhy’s post-second world war drama Woman Unknown, which also won the Golden Lion award for best film.
Jury president Maggie Gyllenhaal said the judges had been able to relax Venice rules around not awarding more than one prize per film because the vote for Arcel had been unanimous.

After her triumph, the 30-year-old actor revealed in interviews with Danish media that she had returned to Denmark after her film’s premiere to sign on at the job centre, as she is on unemployment benefits when not working on films. She then returned to the Lido after being told it would be wise to be present at the awards gala.
In the UK, actors’ trade union Equity said in a 2023 report that 63% of its members have been in receipt of social security at some point in their life.

articles.title: Ed Sheeran says it was 'not my decision' to drop Macklemore from tour
articles.summary: The star says tour promoters took the decision, after Macklemore made pro-Palestinian statements on stage.
body: Ed Sheeran has posted a long statement on Instagram, saying it was not his decision to drop Macklemore from his current US tour.
The US rapper - whose real name is Benjamin Haggerty - was ejected from the line-up after making pro-Palestinian statements at two dates in New Jersey.
His comments drew criticism from Jewish groups, after which some venues put pressure on the tour promoters to have him removed from the line-up.

In his statement, external, Sheeran said he had spoken with the venues "at length all week to try and build a bridge" - but the promoters, Messina Touring Group, had ultimately decided to remove Macklemore from the bill.

articles.title: James McNeill Whistler review – painter’s work shines through attention-grabbing life story
articles.summary: The latest Exhibition on Screen documentary does a good job balancing the famous scandals with the subtle brilliance of his art. Timed to coincide with Tate Britain’s impressive gallery show – which closes at the end of September, so you haven’t long if you’ve missed it so far – this latest from…
body: The only downside is that, so delicate and subtle is his work, Whistler’s shimmering proto-modern visions are perhaps let down a little by pointing a camera at them; it’s hardly the film-maker’s fault but they just don’t jump out of the screen as they do in the gallery. Nevertheless, the film itself is an excellent primer to one of the greats, whose richness of artistic achievement appears to be getting the comprehensive attention it deserves.

articles.title: How city's market became a CBeebies TV set
articles.summary: The show, filmed in Coventry, aims to help young children explore food through their senses
body: Coventry Market's fruit and vegetable stalls, fish counters and busy walkways have become an unlikely TV set.
Cameras are rolling among shoppers and traders as local children explore unfamiliar foods for a new CBeebies series.
I Can Taste It aims to help three to six-year-olds build confidence in trying different foods through sight, smell, touch, sound and taste.
Presented by Aaron Roach Bridgeman and puppet co-host Zesty, the programme is being filmed at the market, which producers say offers children an authentic environment in which to learn about food.

articles.title: ‘The Shards’ Star Jordan Roth on the Beautiful Irony of His Acting Debut and Leaning Into His Dark Side
articles.summary: The Tony-winning producer unpacks the poetic parallels and critical divergences between himself and his character in his first on-screen role: “Ryan Murphy gave me an opportunity to prove myself.”
body: In the season finale, “Stairway to Heaven,” many of those worst impulses won out. In the end, a gruesome serial killer’s spree, alongside the personal and collective upheaval their presence has wrought, touches Bret (Igby Rigney) and his inner circle in a new, unsettling way with the murder of producer Terry Schaffer (Wes Bentley). The whodunnit cliffhanger, which posits that just about any one of the characters could be the culprit, is the result of a splintering not only from Ellis’ text, but of the friendships and even psyches among this glossy gaggle of ‘80s high school elites.

In the episode’s final moments, set to The Go-Go’s “Our Lips Are Sealed,” the camera pans across a holding room, everyone striking a pose as they await police questioning. And with his stark bleached eyebrows and an electric blue silhouette, Terry’s long-time assistant Steven, played by Jordan Roth, is hard to miss among the fitted shirts, feathered hair, and cigarette smoke.
